Two late tests cost less than a ruined load. If someone confirms their firing temperatures from the maker, supplier, or batch notes before loading, include them in the right kiln.

Kiln A reaches 1180 C and kiln B reaches 1240 C, and a glaze fired at the wrong temperature may fail or damage shelves. If you submitted a test, please check your notes and reply with its firing temperature before loading begins. Any test still unidentified will be held back for a later firing.

If the meter still rises, close the manual shutoff and flag the possible leak for repair; note that the fountain will lose water too. The north timer is off and the south meter is stable. If normal fountain use accounts for the rise, leave the shared pipe open.
files.A/work/759.txt: The north irrigation meter has been rising overnight even though the north timer is off; the south meter is stable. We haven't found the cause yet. The north line shares a pipe with the fountain, so the fountain or a leak may be responsible. For now, please leave the north timer off, water north beds by hand from the south side, and report any wet ground or pooling. We'll close the manual shutoff tonight to test, so the fountain may be off.

files.A/work/549.txt:
Before the morning rush, trust the rack, not the kiosk. Have someone move bikes from the nearly full neighboring rack to this one, then correct the kiosk count to match what is physically docked.

The kiosk says 14 and the rack holds 5. With the last truck manifest unsigned, nothing confirms that the delivery happened, and commuters will arrive expecting bikes that aren't there.

Change course if the driver confirms a drop-off or a recount finds the missing nine.
files.A/work/562.txt: Before the morning rush, have someone count the bikes at the rack and check that they’re usable. Don’t send a truck based on the kiosk reading: 14 bikes can’t fit in five spaces, and the unsigned manifest doesn’t confirm a delivery. Update the kiosk with the verified count. If the check shows too few usable bikes for commuters, move bikes from the nearly full neighboring rack, but only into confirmed open spaces.
files.A/work/748.txt: The bike-share kiosk shows 14 bikes available, but only 5 are at the rack. The last truck manifest is unsigned, so we can’t confirm whether the delivery was completed. If you’re heading out this morning, don’t count on the kiosk total; have a backup if you need to leave on time. If you’re returning a bike, the neighboring rack is nearly full, so check for an open dock or plan to use another station.
